CAFEC care about paper the way we care about coffee. products.title: AeroPress Coffee Maker
products.description:
Using an AeroPress is a super easy way to brew coffee at home. Makes a hearty cup for one. AeroPress coffee is typically sweeter and fuller body and mouthfeel, due to the pressured brew method. 

Included

• Main Chamber

• Plunger With Rubber Seal

• Stirring Paddle

• Measuring Scoop

• Filter Basket

• 100 x Filter Papers

• Instruction/Warranty Book

How to brew! - (check the 4th picture for brew guide) 

Recipe
Ratio: 1:16
Dose: 12.5 grams (3/4 AeroPress scoop) 
Water: 200g (to the top) 
Brew time: 3.30 min 

Step 1 

Place filter paper into AeroPress Lid and secure onto chamber then soak the paper with hot water. Remove lid. Connect the 2-AeroPress pieces together then place upside down (numbers should read upside down) 

Step 2

Grind coffee or if already ground weigh out approx 12-13g (3/4 scoop) into AeroPress

Step 3

Pour boiling water within 10 seconds to reach 200g and then agitate aggressively. Place lid on AeroPress and start your timer. 

Step 4

At 3.00 minutes, carefully flip the AeroPress and place on top of your mug. Gently plunge down. This should take around 20 seconds. Stop plunging when you hear a hissing sound.

Atmos keeps out air, moisture, and odours to stop your beans from ageing out before you’ve enjoyed the whole bag. By twisting the lid back and forth, the vacuum pump sucks air out to prevent oxidation and extends coffee’s shelf life up to 50%.

The matte black stainless steel canister also adds a little more durability to the rough and tumble of kitchen bench life.

About: Sítio Dois Irmãos is a family-run farm in Brazil’s Mantiqueira de Minas region, where coffee production is shaped by generational knowledge and a gradual shift toward quality-focused practices. The farm is operated by the Vilas Boas family, whose work reflects a broader movement within the region toward more intentional and precise coffee production. 

For many years, the farm followed a traditional, volume-driven model. A turning point came in 2013 when the family partnered with the COCARIVE cooperative, gaining access to technical support and a network of quality-focused producers. This relationship encouraged changes in both farming and processing, leading to a more selective and controlled approach. 

Today, the farm is managed by Antônio Vilas Boas’ sons, Allan and Allex, who represent a new generation building on their family’s foundation. Their work centers on careful farm management, including pruning, soil health, and organic fertilization, alongside improved post-harvest practices. 

Sítio Dois Irmãos reflects the steady evolution of Mantiqueira producers—family-led operations refining their methods to produce consistent, high-quality coffees with long-term sustainability in mind.

This lot brings together the production of Álvaro Coli, José Wagner, and Mariana Junqueira, three long-term partners. Each component was selected for its consistent flavour profile and for the producers’ shared commitment to maintaining a sustainable future for the region.

Region: Gahahe, Kayanza  

Elevation: 1800 masl

About: Around 870 smallholder farmers deliver their harvest to Gahahe Washing Station in Burundi's Kayanza region, where coffee is grown alongside family food crops on small farms averaging just 230 trees. Together, their work produces a coffee that reflects both careful farming and meticulous processing. 

Only ripe cherries are selected before being hand sorted and dried slowly in thin layers on raised beds. The coffee is turned regularly and protected from rain and intense afternoon sun, allowing the fruit to dry evenly while developing the rich sweetness and complexity that define a great natural process. 

Beyond harvest, Greenco supports producers with agronomy training, seedling nurseries, organic fertiliser programs and community initiatives that strengthen livelihoods and improve yields. It is a long-term investment in both coffee quality and the future of Burundi's smallholder farming communities.

For Tea Recipe: 
Place 28g of chai into your pot/infuser and top with 400ml of 95 degree water. Steep for two and a half minutes and enjoy.

Home Chai Latte Recipe:
Add 28g (a heaped tablespoon) into the bottom of your pot and top with just enough hot water to cover the leaves. Brew for two or three minutes then add your milk of choice. Warm over a medium heat until steamy. Strain into your favourite mug and sip away.

Chai spice mix (53.2%)[Ginger, Clove, Date Pieces, Star Anise, Cinnamon, Fennel Seed, Rapadura Sugar], Rice Malt Syrup, Black Tea (10.8%), Maple Syrup.

products.title: Colombia | El Vergel Estate | Caturra | Washed Decaf
products.description:
El Vergel Estate sits in Fresno, Tolima, where Elías and Shady Bayter have spent more than a decade refining their approach to coffee. What began as a family farm has grown into Forest Coffee, a network connecting more than 250 coffee-growing families through a focus on quality, innovation and transparent trade.
 
This lot is naturally decaffeinated using the sugarcane process in Colombia. Green coffee is gently steamed before caffeine is removed with naturally derived ethyl acetate from sugarcane. The beans are then steamed again to remove any remaining residue, preserving the coffee's sweetness, structure and origin character while reducing caffeine by 99%.
 
The result is a decaf that drinks like coffee first, decaf second. Sweet, balanced and full of flavour, without compromising the character that makes Colombian coffee so enjoyable.

About: Finca El Ángel is the sixth and most recent addition to the Silva family’s operation, acquired in December 2022. The farm was originally established in 2018 by the Mathies family, who processed their coffees at the Silva family mill in Apeneca. After tasting the first harvest in late 2021, Rafael Jr. and the Mathies family agreed on a sale, bringing El Ángel into the Silva portfolio. 

Set high on the slopes of the Santa Ana volcano, El Ángel is planted exclusively with coffee. Five varieties are cultivated: Red Bourbon, Orange Bourbon, Pacamara, SL-28 and Geisha. 

The farm is now in a period of transition. Rafa is renovating and refining the original vision while maintaining sufficient production to ensure long term viability. Progress can be steady and at times slow, though early results suggest the direction is sound. In 2024, a naturally processed SL-28 from El Ángel placed second in the Natural category at the El Salvador Cup of Excellence.

 SL-28, developed in Kenya, is recognised for pronounced sweetness and vibrant acidity. This lot was traditionally washed, highlighting its structured, juicy profile.

About: Finca La Siberia has been in the Silva family since 1870. Named for its chaotic climate and the challenging trails that lead to it, Siberia is a beautiful but often harsh and unforgiving place. 

With knowledge and experience passed down over six generations, the Silva family has transformed Siberia into one of the most renowned estates in El Salvador. Today, the family grows a range of varieties, including Bourbon, Pacamara, SL-34 and Geisha. 

As his parents begin to slow down and enjoy some well-earned time with their grandchildren, Rafael Jr. now manages the day-to-day operations across all the family farms, while also overseeing processing at the mill. Keen to blend a traditional approach learned from his father with a spirit of experimentation, Rafa understands that great coffee does not happen by accident. He is meticulous in his picking, processing and drying protocols, carefully tracking each day’s harvest from tree to export. 

This washed Bourbon is clean, sweet and approachable — a wonderful example of Salvadoran coffee.

About: The Caballero family are legendary in Honduras. For generations, they have produced exceptional coffee around the town of Marcala in La Paz, western Honduras, near the border with El Salvador. 

It is no understatement to say Fabio Caballero Jr has coffee in his blood. A fifth-generation producer, he is already demonstrating the depth of skill and focus that has defined the Caballero name for decades. 

After graduating from university, Fabio began managing several of his family’s farms and, in 2019, founded Finca La Salvaje with his grandfather, Don Fabio Caballero, winner of the 2018 Honduras Cup of Excellence. La Salvaje is planted with Geisha and Java, grown from seed sourced from the family’s Cup of Excellence-winning farm, Finca San Francisco. 

The name La Salvaje, meaning “wild” in Spanish, reflects the untamed environment in which the coffee is grown, rich with birdlife, native flora, and natural shade. This coffee was the highest-scoring lot in the 2025 Honduras Cup of Excellence, earning 91.59 points, placing first in the Exotic category, and achieving the highest auction price at USD 88.40 per pound.

products.title: Honduras | Manuel Vallecillo | Pacas | Washed
products.description:
Region: El Cielito, Santa Barbara

Elevation: 1650 masl

About: Proud Mary’s connection to the Santa Barbara region of Honduras began all the way back in 2012, when we were introduced to a small group of producers situated around the town of Peña Blanca, close to the shores of the stunning Lake Yojoa. More than a decade later, that group of producers has grown in number, and our relationships have deepened.

Manuel Vallecillo was born in Nueva Esperanza, near Santa Barbara. From a young age, he worked in coffee production and learnt as much as possible. Years later, Manuel moved to the US, but in 2014 coffee called him back, and he purchased Finca Los Primos in the mountains of Santa Barbara.

The farm is planted exclusively with the Pacas variety, which is native to El Salvador but thrives in the microclimate surrounding Manuel’s farm. Manuel now splits his time between Texas and El Cielito, spending the harvest season at the farm and the rest of the year in Houston, Texas, with his family.

This coffee continues to impress us on the cupping table each year. The current harvest is complex and silky, with notes of yellow plum and black tea.

products.title: Honduras | Ovidio Gomez | Geisha | Honey
products.description:

About: Proud Mary’s connection to the Santa Barbara region of Honduras began all the way back in 2012, when we were introduced to a small group of producers situated around the town of Peña Blanca, close to the shores of the stunning Lake Yojoa. More than a decade later, that group of producers has grown in number, and our relationships have deepened.

Ovidio Gomez was among the members of that initial group. A man of few words, he has a gruff exterior, often with a machete in hand, but beneath it is a passionate care for the land and his community. Ovidio’s coffees have developed a strong following among our staff and regular customers, with each new release eagerly anticipated.

With a relationship spanning more than ten years, it would be easy to assume there are no firsts left to uncover. This year proves otherwise. For the first time, we are excited to share a Geisha from Ovidio Gomez. It stood out immediately on the cupping table during our most recent trip to Honduras, a compelling expression of Santa Barbara Geisha.

products.title: Panama | Bambito Estate | Geisha | Washed
products.description:
Altitude: 1660 – 1800 masl

About: Bambito Estate has been passed down through five generations of the Amar Sittón family. The patriarch of the family, Alberto Sittón Ríos, acquired the farm from his father in 1945 and it remained his lifelong passion. Today, Bambito Estate is run by Priscilla, her brother Rafael, and her son Ivan.   

Located high up in the cloudy forests of Volcan Baru, Bambito Estate is nestled between two national parks and is intersected by two mountain ridges running from east to west, creating two distinct microclimates for coffee cultivation. This unique setting produces Geisha that few places on Earth can match, boasting a clear sparkling acidity and strongly perfumed florals. We have had the privilege of knowing the Amar Sittón family since our first trip to Panama in 2010. At that time, they weren't producing enough Geisha to sell, but we recognized they had something truly special. Since their first exportable harvest in 2013, we have been purchasing Geisha coffee from Bambito Estate, and it consistently remains one of our favorites each year.

Elevation: 1600-2100 masl

About: Graciano Cruz is something of an enigma. A scientist, coffee producer, party animal, visionary, and ecologist. It is difficult to define him precisely. He is a wild operator, working across multiple disciplines with a clear sense of curiosity and intent. In addition to his two farms in Panama, Graciano also operates in El Salvador and has contributed to projects in other coffee-producing regions such as Ethiopia, Peru, Taiwan, and Brazil. Amongst this breadth of work, he continues to produce coffees at a high level, most recently placing 6th in the Best of Panama competition. 

The highest sections of Los Lajones sit at around 2,100 metres above sea level. It is in these upper elevations that Graciano’s Geisha grows within native cloud forest. This lot comes from a section known as Bambu. 

Prior to the 2024 harvest, Graciano had exclusively processed his coffees using honey or natural methods. Seeking a new direction, he began trialling washed processing. This lot reflects that shift, presenting a structured profile with florals and citrus, alongside the more developed tropical characteristics often associated with his work.

5 single servings of Benti Nenka Ethiopia.

This exceptional coffee comes from the Benti Nenka washing station, located in a small village – also called Benti Nenka – in Guji. Farming practices in Guji remain pretty traditional, with producers typically farming very small plots of land (1-2 hectares) adjacent to their homes – they’re essentially farming in their backyard. It’s very much a family business, with spouses, children, and grandchildren providing all the labor. After the days harvest is done, producers deliver their coffee to community washing stations for processing.  

Almost 600 producers deliver their coffee to the Benti Nenka washing station, where Amare Tesfaye (the Station Manager) and his team work their processing magic. Focusing mostly on natural processing, coffees are thoroughly sorted before being dried on raised beds in the sun. The fertile soil and high altitude in the region provide the perfect conditions for exceptional coffee.
